stem:
During a storm, strong wind blows fast over the tin roof of Farhan's house. The air inside the house below the roof is still.

Why can the roof be lifted?

options.text: The fast-moving air above the roof has lower pressure, so the higher pressure of the still air below pushes the roof upward.
The fast-moving air above the roof has higher pressure, so that higher pressure pushes the roof upward from above.
The roof lifts even when the pressure of the still air below equals the pressure of the fast-moving air above.
The pressure above the roof is lower simply because it is above, whether the air is moving or still.

teacher.key_rationale: Fast air above the roof has lower pressure; higher pressure of still air below can lift the roof. B reverses the speed–pressure link. C drops the need for higher pressure on the opposite side. D judges from being above rather than from air speed.
